summary: The UI follow-up to encrypted phone transport, built to the approved mock. The desktop's Devices & machines tab shows the short certificate fingerprint (first 8 lowercase hex of the pinned SHA-256) beside the QR. Both phones show the same machine-row anatomy: status dot, name, short fingerprint for pinned rows, then a lock and Encrypted, Not encrypted, local only, or Cloud IAP, then the address in mono. Rows are split into Live (N of M) and Needs attention. A remote ws:// row the build refuses is amber with a hint and Scan new QR and Use Cloud IAP (no retry). A row whose certificate changed is red: iOS shows the hint inline with Scan QR again and Remove; Android opens a sheet with the reinstall case, the interception warning with the fingerprint sentence, Scan QR again, Remove machine and Not now before any scanner. A wss:// row without a pin reads Encrypted with a lock and no fingerprint. Scan again replaces the saved machine instead of adding a second one, and a release or store build refuses a rescanned plain ws:// QR to another computer before it replaces anything: the scanner stays open with the refusal. On iOS a scanned or typed QR without a certificate pin opens the QR from an older Switchboard sheet instead of saving. Rules and copy live in src/shared/connection-security.ts; Android keeps a copy checked against tests/fixtures/connection-security-copy.json.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing new is stored. Row states are derived from the saved address (its fp parameter) and in-memory connection state. A scan again rewrites the existing saved machine through the existing edit path (Expo updateConnection, Android PairingSaveIntent.Edit), so no schema or migration changes.

automated: vitest tests/unit/connection-security.test.ts: short fingerprint, fp in a URL, the row-state order (IAP, certificate changed, refused, pinned, local, encrypted, plain), Needs attention, the fingerprint and lock rules, placeholder filling, and the copy fixture equal to the shared copy.

jest apps/mobile MachineRow.test.tsx: pinned, local, IAP, refused and certificate-changed rows render the mock anatomy, copy and buttons (no retry on a refused row), and the old QR sheet renders its title, address, two options and Cancel.

Gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest: ConnectionSecurityTest (rules and every Android string equal to the fixture), ConnectionRowPolicyTest (sections and status detail), ConnectionsPresentationTest (security, short fingerprint and address per row), RuntimeConnectionsMapperTest (only a certificate mismatch marks a row), ConnectionsAccessibilityPolicyTest, PairingFormPolicyTest (a scan again edits the machine and keeps its name, and a release rescan refuses a plain ws:// QR to another computer), ConnectionDecisionsTest.
jest apps/mobile transport-gate.test.ts: a rescan waits for the build type, so a store build refuses a plain ws:// QR before it replaces the saved address.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.
